sections.h2: How fast can a Colleyville home be sold?
sections.html:
A cash purchase can wrap up on a schedule you set, while a standard listing in a city of expensive homes tends to take longer and may bring more. Colleyville owners weigh both.

Colleyville is in northeastern Tarrant County, and nearly every household owns its home. That leaves few investor-owned rentals and a market of larger, long-held houses.

  • Cash purchase: the house is taken as it stands, with no showings or lender delays.
  • Listing: the best route for a house in strong condition, with inspections and negotiated repairs.
  • Private sale: workable with a written contract and a title company.

sections.h2: How does Colleyville measure up in the QuickFacts data?
sections.html:
They describe a wealthy, settled city. QuickFacts shows 25,727 people on the July 1, 2025 estimate, a 1.2% dip from the April 2020 base, and counts 9,072 households averaging 2.86 people.

Mortgaged owners pay a median of $4,000+ a month in housing costs, and owners with no mortgage $1,500+. Persons in poverty are 2.5%, and 94.1% of residents kept the same address from the prior year, so houses seldom change hands. One resident in five is at least 65, which makes estate settlement and downsizing frequent reasons to sell.

The Handbook of Texas says the area was first settled in the 1850s and grew from small communities named Spring Garden, Pleasant Run, Pleasant Glade and Red Rock, later Bransford. A physician, Hilburn Howard Colley, settled in Bransford and his name was attached to a community around a store founded in 1914, becoming Coleysville and later Colleyville.

The entry says growth came mainly from proximity to Fort Worth, where most residents worked. Colleyville was incorporated on January 10, 1956, had 1,491 residents by 1964, and counted 12,724 in 1990 and 19,636 in 2000. In the early 1980s the town divided over whether to allow only costly single-family homes on large lots or smaller lots and multifamily housing.

That debate helps explain today's mix: large lots, high values and few rentals. Land area is 13.12 square miles, and density in 2020 was 1,986.2 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What does the economy around Colleyville look like?
sections.html:
The Handbook says Colleyville's growth came mostly from nearness to Fort Worth, where most residents worked, and QuickFacts shows the same commuting pattern with a 24.1 minute average trip. The city lies on State Highway 26, and the entry notes that a St. Louis Southwestern rail line crossed the community without driving its growth.

  • Veterans: 1,443 residents.
  • Foreign-born residents: 11.4%.
  • Households with broadband: 99.3%.
  • Residents under 65 without health insurance: 3.2%.
  • 2022 retail sales: $417,097 thousand, or $16,130 per person.
  • Medical and social-service receipts in 2022: $152,616 thousand.
  • Freight and storage receipts in 2022: $108,671 thousand.

Those totals describe businesses inside the city. Ask the appraisal district how commercial parcels near your street are valued, since they share the same taxing units.

sections.h2: What should a Colleyville seller gather first?
sections.html: Collect the paperwork that closing will call for. A copy of your deed, the most recent appraisal notice, proof of any homestead or over-65 exemption, and a tax certificate cover most questions. For an inherited house, add the court order, executor's letters or recorded deed that shows who may sign. Gathering these early shortens the time between offer and closing.

sections.h2: How do Colleyville schools and neighbors affect a sale?
sections.html:
Families shopping for larger homes check schools early. Colleyville Heritage High School belongs to Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District and describes itself as a UIL 5A school with a National Blue Ribbon designation and the Panthers as its mascot.

QuickFacts reinforces why: 99.1% of adults over 25 finished high school, 69.1% completed a four-year degree or more, and workers spend 24.1 minutes getting to their jobs. The Handbook places the city north of Bedford and south of Southlake, with Grapevine and Euless to the east, a useful way to describe the location to out-of-area buyers.

sections.h2: What are the Tarrant County tax dates for a Colleyville owner?
sections.html:
The county tax office has bills going out around October 1, with January 31 the last day before delinquency and February 1 the day penalty and interest start. Penalty begins at 6 percent and climbs monthly to 12 percent in July, while interest adds 1 percent monthly.

On July 1 delinquent accounts move to tax attorneys, who can add up to 20 percent. Half payments are due November 30 and June 30, and the quarterly plan for older and disabled owners runs from January through July. Exemption filings at Tarrant Appraisal District close April 30 and protests May 15.

sections.h2: How is a homestead exemption filed with Tarrant Appraisal District?
sections.html:
Filing is free. You can use the district's online form or print form 50-114 and mail or email it. A Texas driver's license or ID with the home address is required.

Someone who buys and moves in can claim the exemption from the move-in date when the previous owner had none that year. The exemption also caps yearly appraisal growth at 10 percent, with exceptions for improvements and added land.

Heir property needs an ownership affidavit, the prior owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation, and each other heir living there signs an authorization.

sections.h2: How do exemptions for older owners work here?
sections.html: With a fifth of residents 65 or older, many Colleyville owners hold a school tax ceiling. The Comptroller describes an extra school exemption of $60,000 and says the ceiling can follow the owner to another Texas homestead. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older may keep it. Ask the district before selling whether yours would transfer.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes when a Colleyville house closes?
sections.html: The title company splits the year between buyer and seller. A lien attaches every January 1, and the Comptroller says the January owner remains liable. If back taxes exist, the closing agent pays them from sale funds, so ask the county for a tax certificate before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: Can heirs sell a Colleyville house quickly?
sections.html: They can once title is clear. Texas allows four years after death to probate a will, and a small estate affidavit is limited to $75,000 excluding the homestead. Other routes are a muniment of title, an executor's deed, or a transfer on death deed recorded in the owner's lifetime. An heirship affidavit is just a sworn statement, which a buyer may refuse to rely on.

sections.h2: What if a Colleyville borrower falls behind?
sections.html: Texas servicers generally wait until a loan is over 120 days delinquent. A default notice gives 20 days to reinstate, and the sale notice follows with an auction no sooner than 21 days later, on a first Tuesday. Closing a sale first avoids the auction.

faqs.q: Is selling without an agent common in Colleyville?
faqs.a: It can work for a house in sound condition and you can manage showings and paperwork. A title company still prepares the deed and splits the tax year.

faqs.q: When does a Colleyville buyer get the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: From the move-in date, when the seller had not claimed one that year, according to Tarrant Appraisal District.

faqs.q: Where is a Colleyville protest filed?
faqs.a: At Tarrant Appraisal District, by May 15 for the current year according to the county tax office dates page.

faqs.q: What if taxes on a Colleyville house are late?
faqs.a: Penalty climbs monthly to 12 percent in July and interest adds 1 percent monthly, so request the payoff amount from the county; closing usually settles it.

faqs.q: Can an heir sign a Colleyville deed before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not. The buyer's title company wants a court order, an executor's authority or a recorded transfer on death deed.
